newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end up, led by properties, banks.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end up, led by properties, banks.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended higher for the third day in a row on Friday, with a rally in property and bank stocks keeping the Hang Seng Index well above 13,000 points, although momentum began to slow after a strong week.
The Hang Seng ended 60.92 points, or 0.47 percent, higher at 13,081.70 after reaching a session high of 13,145.93. The index put on 435.94 points, or 3.45 percent, this week.
Turnover was HK$13.77 billion compared with HK$12.50 billion on Thursday.
"I think the overall market has resumed its uptrend after the last few weeks of consolidation," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.

"Worries over rising interest rates have subsided because of the mild inflationary pressure in the U.S. Immediate resistance is now at 13,200 points. Once it pierces through 13,200 then the next stop is 14,000 again," said Tang.
However, momentum seemed to slow on Friday after strong gains in the two previous sessions and ahead of U.S. April employment data due later.
"It is going to slow as it gets well past the 13,000 level," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Mansion House Research analyst Henry Lui said some investors had begun to take profits in the blue-chip counters.
"I think the market will slightly consolidate next week. You will see the market trade around 12,700 to 13,200," he said.

Property stocks led the rise on Friday, with shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd jumping HK$1.25 to HK$70.75, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd adding HK$1.00 to HK$87.50 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd rising HK$1.25 to HK$67.50.
"Property counters were the hardest hit when interest rates moved higher and if rates are steady we will probably see a recovery in the property market and property stocks," said Tang.
Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc jumped to a record high at HK$198.00 before closing the session at HK$197.50, up HK$2.50.
Some red chips succumbed to profit-taking, with Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd finishing down HK$1.00 at HK$43.20 and China Resources Enterprise Ltd easing HK$0.30 at HK$21.85.
"All of the red chips could fall 10 or 15 percent and you could still only say it is a natural correction after their steep rise," said Rossiter.
The H-share index fell 6.17 points to 1,068.21.
But selected H-shares moved higher with Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd adding HK$0.10 to HK$1.32 and Jingwei Textile Machinery Co Ltd up HK$0.10 at HK$1.32.
